title: Incremental erase coordinator for attribute-shredding and derived-analytics backfills
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Our analytics pipelines currently perform coarse-grained PII scrubbing during ingestion (redaction of whole event blobs) which makes selective removals and attribute-level deletions downstream difficult. Customers and auditors increasingly ask for fine-grained deletion semantics: remove specific attributes (email, phone, credit_card_last4) from historical analytic aggregates and derived datasets without invalidating entire rows or losing non-PII signals.

This ticket introduces an Incremental Erase Coordinator (IEC) that orchestrates attribute-level shredding across streaming and batch analytic layers, ensures deletion propagation to derived datasets, and provides auditable proofs of action. The IEC must support: incremental backfills, consistency checks between source and derived assets, idempotent operations, and safe rollout with canaries and throttling.

Scope: prototype coordinator service + pipeline connectors for Segments-analytics, BigQuery-style warehouse views, and pre-aggregation materialized tables. Implement signing/audit ledger entries for each deletion job, add a consistency diff job that verifies deleted attribute absence, and expose a console endpoint for customers to request attribute-shred operations and track progress.

Out of scope: client SDK changes, full legal attestation flow (this ticket produces artifacts used by legal-runbook work).
acceptance_criteria:
- IEC deployed to staging and can run an attribute-shred job targeting a single attribute (e.g., user.email) across streaming daily shards and a single derived materialized table.
- Jobs are idempotent: re-running the same job key must not re-delete or corrupt non-target fields.
- Audit ledger entries (job id, requestor, hash of attribute name, time range, affected tables) are emitted to the compliance topic.
- Consistency diff job detects remaining occurrences (if any) and reports zero for canary datasets before production rollout.
- End-to-end test demonstrating a customer-initiated attribute removal request through the console API and visibility in the console job UI.
design_notes:
High-level design: IEC is a small coordinator service (stateless) that schedules deletion tasks and tracks their lifecycle in a durable job store. Tasks are executed by existing pipeline workers through a deletion task consumer. Each deletion task carries: canonical job id, attribute selector (path expression), dataset selectors, start/end time window, and a signed deletion token for authorization.

Shredding approach: write-only 'shred' transformers that emit patch records to a deletion topic; downstream table mutators apply in-place attribute redaction using SQL UPDATE/REPLACE semantics where supported, or create shadowed delta slices for append-only stores. For aggregate tables, we prefer reversible re-aggregation: replay raw events with attribute removed into a new materialization partition rather than attempting in-place numeric corrections.

Consistency and verification: after mutators finish, IEC triggers a diff-runner to sample keys and run attribute-existence queries. If the diff exceeds a tolerance threshold, IEC marks job as FAILED and opens a corrective backfill.

Security: deletion job requests require KMS-signed request tokens issued by console. Audit ledger entries are hashed and include a merkle-root style proof to make tampering detectable.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy IEC to staging with feature flag 'iec_enabled'. 2) Run on synthetic canary dataset and validate canary metrics. 3) Enable for one low-traffic customer as pilot; run daily for a week. 4) Gradually enable across more customers with throttling and rate limits. 5) After 2-week pilot, promote to production and monitor for 4 weeks.

Operational guardrails: max parallel deletions per org: 2, per-cluster concurrency: 10, automatic abort if job error rate > 2% for > 30 minutes.
telemetry: Emit the following metrics to observability: job_started, job_succeeded, job_failed, tasks_queued, tasks_completed, consistency_diff_count, patched_rows_count, bytes_scanned, average_task_latency_ms. Tag metrics with org_id, job_id, attribute_hash, pipeline_type (streaming/batch). Emit audit ledger events to compliance topic with schema version v1.
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator state transitions. Integration tests: staging run over 7-day shard window with synthetic PII attributes; assert patched_rows_count equals expected, and diff-runner reports zero. Chaos test: simulate mutator worker restarts during a job and verify idempotence. Regression test: ensure unrelated fields for same rows remain unchanged. Add e2e test that triggers deletion from console API and polls job status until success.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: accidental over-deletion due to incorrect path selector. Mitigation: require review step for selectors that match > 1000 distinct user keys; require manual approval for wildcard selectors in production.
Risk: long-running re-aggregation costs. Mitigation: provide cost-estimate in UI before confirming job; support dry-run to sample re-aggregation size.
Risk: inconsistent state between streaming and batch. Mitigation: IEC coordinates cutoff watermark and waits for stream to catch up before mutator run; run consistency diff and block job completion until within tolerance.
